title_authority: No official title supplied; the user asked for "my chess program" (2026-10-31). The program calls itself CISAB (line 10: CISAB A COMPUTER CHESS GAME IN BASIC; title screen C I S A B). CISAB is BASIC spelled backwards.
order_evidence: Inferred development sequence, not established dates. v01 and v02 are tape1b saves 8 and 10; v03-v07 are tape13a saves 9-13; v08-v14 are tape13b saves 1-6 and 8, each in save order. Each listing is the previous one with changes, and v03 starts from v02's code (its lines 10-57 and most of the move generator are v02's). The archive labels V2-V9 were assigned by the recovery from save order; they are not in the programs. No save is dated. Tape numbers alone do not establish chronology.
context: User note in the recovery archive (programs-to-find.md): "Chess program — one I competed with in Peoria." From v03 on the program asks WHAT COLOR ARE WE and WHAT WAS THEIR ... MOVE, i.e. an operator relays an opponent's moves.
